text:
anna: heads-up — hawthorn-9b-v2 (int4) canary nodes hit OOM after warmup, reproducing on two hosts.
leo: saw alert. any logs/snippets? where in the sequence does it fail?
anna: small snippet: fails ~token 820-930 on multi-turn requests, not a single giant prompt.
```
[2025-11-02T14:12:03Z] OOMError allocate(1.2GB) failed
model=hawthorn-9b-v2-int4 node=canary-ml-07
kv_cache_usage=0.84 fragmentation_est=0.28
batch_size=4 latency=95ms max_new_tokens=512
```
sam: likely interaction between int4 memory layout and continuous batching + prefetch. increases transient KV pressure.
maria: did we see a quality regression from int4 quant? we onboarded int4 artifacts yesterday right?
anna: yes, small long-form delta: ~-0.9% on our QA slice. int8 looked fine.
david: reminds me of cedar10b case — long max_new_tokens + higher concurrency caused slab fragmentation and OOMs. fix then was conservative defaults + kv eviction.
anna: current canary config: 
```
model: hawthorn-9b-v2-int4
batching:
  max_batch_size: 8
  batch_window_ms: 20
prefetch: true
max_new_tokens: 512
kv_eviction: off
soft_eviction_threshold: 0.9
```
leo: propose minimal mitigation: 1) max_new_tokens -> 256 2) max_batch_size -> 4 3) enable kv_eviction trim_percent=0.12 4) disable prefetch on canary to avoid transient spikes
maria: agree. also we should re-run quant vs int8 slices focused on multi-turn prompts. if quality delta >1.5% fallback to int8.
sam: i'll run a quick bench on canary after the change, post numbers in ~30m.
deploy-bot: deploy request queued: hawthorn-int4-canary-patch-20251102 by anna. Applying in 5m.
anna: patch applied to small canary now. if stable, widen to dedicated pool with 50/50 A/B.
david: also suggest enabling slot_compactor background sweep (interval=60s) to reduce fragmentation; low risk.
leo: +1 but add tracing to monitor p95 impact.
anna: bench after patch: 
```
config: max_new_tokens=256, max_batch_size=4, prefetch=false, kv_eviction=enabled
throughput: 2350 req/min (+3% vs int8 smallbatch)
latency p50: 92ms p95: 220ms
OOMs: 0 (ran ~2k reqs across 3 nodes)
quality delta vs int8: -0.4% (long-turn)
```
maria: OOMs resolved and quality hit reduced — acceptable for canary. schedule 24h drift checks and run eval every 6h for 24h.
sam: canary at 10% traffic with auto-quality monitoring. rule: >1% regression sustained for 3hrs -> auto-fallback to int8.
david: follow-up: create model-specific safe profile: max_new_tokens=256, batch_window_ms=12, kv_eviction=on, slot_compactor=60s.
anna: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/ml-profiles/pull/412 (tests included).
leo: also add per-token memory trend traces on canary dashboards to help distinguish leak vs fragmentation.
maria: +1. add 24h cost-per-token bench vs int8 to confirm unit economics.
anna: summary: applied conservative defaults, OOMs gone, small quality delta reduced. follow-ups: profile PR, enable slot_compactor, dashboard traces, auto-fallback rule. :thumbsup:
leo: will monitor fragmentation and p95. ping if it regresses.
anna: thanks all!
